newsitem.title: USA: NCR aims to boost revs, margins in 1997.
newsitem.headline: NCR aims to boost revs, margins in 1997.

text.p: NCR Corp said Tuesday it made progress during the fourth quarter of 1996 in cutting expenses and boosting gross margins, and was focused now on bolstering revenues and margins for the coming year.

In a statement accompanying the relase of NCR's earnings, Lars Nyberg, NCR's chairman and chief executive, said the company acheived its 1996 year goal of break-even operating results on flat revenues in its core operations.
"The challenge for NCR is very clear now; we must achieve growth in revenue and gross margins," Nyberg said.
NCR said its gross profit margins rose 7.2 percentage points year-over-year to 30.1 percent in the fourth quarter.
However, the increase was aided by a provision for restructuring in the fourth quarter of 1995 and the release of restructuring reserves in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Excluding these restructuring amounts from both periods, gross margins in the fourth quarter of 1996 were 29.6 percent, up 5.6 percentage points over the comparable period of 1995.
It said operating expenses in the fourth quarter were $488 million compared to $706 million in the year ago period, a decrease of $218 million.
When the impact of restructuring is excluded from both periods, expenses declined by $149 million, or 22 percent.
NCR began trading as an independent public company earlier this month.

During its final quarter as a subsidiary of AT&T, NCR reported fourth-quarter net income of $7 million, or $.07 per share, compared to a net loss of $305 million, or $3.01 per share, in the comparable period last year.
The net effect of certain restructuring-related adjustments in the 1996 fourth quarter cut net income by $27 million, or $0.27 per share, it said.
Revenue in the quarter was $2.04 billion, down 10 percent from the $2.27 billion a year ago.
NCR blamed the revenue decline primarily on its decision to exit the mass-market PC and entry-level server businesses.
For core operations geographically, fourth quarter order increases were led by substantial gains in the Asia/Pacific region and by very good gains in the Americas region.
Revenue in the quarter from core operations increased three percent from a year ago, and rose five percent on a local currency basis.
On a product line basis, revenue for its faster growing computer products business rose 25 percent in the quarter and revenue for financial products gained 12 percent.
The Asia/Pacific region reported a decline in revenue of three percent for the quarter, principally due to the strengthening of the dollar against the yen.
Thanks to a genorous divestiture dowry from AT&T Corp, NCR ended 1996 with $1.2 billion in cash and debt of $76 million. At December 31, it employed 38,600 people, including contractors.
